† marks proposed/target API not yet in current code.
Receiver (&self / &mut self) is implicit in the lifeline.
Compilation internals (Sched, Cache, Backend, etc.) delegated to exec-flow-compilation —
this diagram shows REPL orchestration around register_module + wait_for_inmem_codegen + eval + trampoline.
Display formatting (format_eval_result, pretty_print, write_prompt, print_banner) is a method group on Sess —
not a separate facade.
STARTUP — parse cli args, construct session, register entry module (no wait), init watcher, print banner
(entry module in-mem catches up at the first iteration's wait_for_inmem_codegen.
Other transitively imported modules — including any prelude — are pulled in via the import branch of exec-flow-compilation.
The REPL never references the prelude directly.)
per repl/spec.md §0 — Action ∈ { Repl, Run, Link, Version, Help }.
This diagram covers Action::Repl. For Run / Link see exec-flow-run, exec-flow-link.
ProjectTarget { project_root: PathBuf, entry_module: ModuleFullPath } resolved per repl/spec.md §0.5.
spawns priority + nice worker pools — opens cache directory — initialises empty SymbolTables.
Watcher channel opened separately by init_watcher (after register_module, so the entry module's path is known)
registers the entry module under target.entry_module (defaults to "user" if no positional arg).
See exec-flow-compilation. Fire-and-forget, returns immediately. Compilation begins in background.
opens the OS file watcher on project_root, wires channel to the background watcher event processor (created suspended)
REPL session state — current_repl_module: ModuleFullPath = target.entry_module
(this is THE module that defns and imports append to. Changeable via /mod. Defaults to entry module.
"user" is just the default name when no positional arg is given — it is not architecturally special.)
LOOP ITERATION — per-input cycle
(repeats until /quit or EOF)
STEP 1 — resume watcher processing
(events flow during the prompt-wait window)
active=true — Sess background processor pulls events from the watcher channel and invokes re_register_module per event
STEP 2 — print prompt and block on user input
(while LineEditor is blocked, watcher events may arrive and be processed concurrently)
background watcher processor pulls the event and invokes re_register_module —
typecheck + JIT proceed without blocking the LineEditor read
see exec-flow-compilation watcher branch
[each event (concurrent with LineEditor blocking)]
[one or more file changes arrive during the prompt-wait]
[until balanced]
[parens unbalanced AND input does not start with "/" (slash commands are single-line per main.rs)]
STEP 3 — suspend watcher processing
(events arriving from now on accumulate in the channel until next iteration's STEP 1)
active=false — Sess background processor stops pulling events —
any in-flight re_register_module calls complete normally
STEP 4 — catch up in-mem codegen
(blocks until entry module initial load + all watcher-triggered reloads from STEP 2 are in-mem.
This makes /list, /info, eval all see consistent module state.)
STEP 5 — dispatch input via process_commands
process_commands handles slash commands directly (writing some output to stdout for streaming commands) —
routes /quit to CommandResult::Quit, blank/comment to CommandResult::Nothing,
/list /info /sig /exports etc. to CommandResult::Final(text) via introspection accessors,
Cranelisp source to CommandResult::Compile(src) for the caller to feed into eval.
no display, no eval — proceed to STEP 7
break out of loop — see SHUTDOWN below
writes the slash-command's output to stdout
eval internals (per pipeline-v4 §6.2) —

parse src, classify each form, route through CompilerSession::process_form (the SAME shared orchestrator used by the compilation worker — see exec-flow-compilation typecheck-phase loop body and facades/int.md "process_form — the gap-orchestration retry loop").

process_form catches ExpansionError::Gap / CheckError::Gap returns from frontend and typecheck, dispatches via handle_gap (register + wait_for_typecheck_symbol + (priority_boost + wait_for_inmem) + wait_for_typecheck_type as needed), and retries until expand and check_form both succeed.
For definition forms, eval follows up with insert_symbol to commit additively to current_repl_module.
For the trailing expression, eval skips insert_symbol — the temp closure has no module commit — and hands the typed AST to a fresh per-eval JITModule.

shared entry point — invokes the same expand → build_ast → check_form sequence shown in exec-flow-compilation typecheck-phase loop body, including the gap-orchestration retry loop for any FQ refs the input touches. scope = current_repl_module supplies typecheck visibility (locals + imports + private symbols). No commit yet.
additive commit — internally calls SymbolTable::insert_or_update on ST_current.
Triggers any pending typecheck waiters and (if needs_codegen) enqueues a Jit work item.
per-symbol wait — block only on the new symbol's jit, not on every pending in-mem item (global wait already happened at STEP 4)
[needs_codegen]
for defn redefinition — Decision 31 reclaims old Arc<Jit> when previous ModuleEntry's Code is dropped
[one or more definition forms (defn / defmacro / deftype / deftrait / impl / import / mod / platform / def)]
same shared entry point and same gap-orchestration retry loop — FQ refs in the expression are resolved by process_form before it returns.
scope = current_repl_module for visibility, no commit target.
The wrapped expression is "(defn __expr [] expr)" but __expr is NOT committed anywhere — no insert_symbol call follows.
The temp closure exists only as a typed AST + per-eval JIT until the trampoline returns and the JIT drops.
enqueues BlockingJitCodegen for dep (priority-boosted) and waits — see exec-flow-compilation
[each un-codegenned dependency dep: FQSymbol in callees]
per pipeline-v4 §6.2 — fresh JITModule per eval call.
Wrapped in Jit newtype whose Drop calls unsafe JITModule::free_memory() (Decision 31).
Temp closure has NO entry in ST_current and NO GOT slot — it is one-shot.

Per Decision 41 backend writes Code::Jit { jit, ptr } directly via SymbolTable::write_code (or, for the temp-closure case, directly into a one-shot in-process slot — int reads code_ptr from the populated entry below).
runtime cadence active inside the call —
atomic RC inc/dec, fork-join cells (lenient eval / par bind!),
IO trampoline if expected_type wraps IO _ (see exec-flow-runtime)
drop(Jit) — custom Drop calls unsafe JITModule::free_memory() —
__expr's executable memory is reclaimed before the next iteration
(safety holds because the value is fully consumed, GOT was never updated, and fn values are heap closures that go through GOTs not raw ptrs)
[trailing expression form (e.g. "(+ 1 2)" or "factorial 10")]
formats per repl/spec.md §1 — ":Type value — classification — docstring" for definitions, bare ":Type value" for expressions, etc.
per repl/spec.md §15 — persists current_repl_module's accumulated forms to {project_root}/{current_repl_module}.cl
[result is a definition or structural change]
[CommandResult::Nothing]
STEP 6 — sync watcher set with newly-loaded modules
(imports during eval may have registered new modules — the watcher should now watch their files too)
STEP 7 — print next prompt with timing info from the just-completed iteration
[until /quit or EOF]
SHUTDOWN — on /quit or EOF
ensures cache .o + sidecars are written for all touched modules — next REPL session can cache-hit
signals worker pools to drain + terminate —
closes watcher channel — closes cache directory.
drop(Sess) — Decision 31 reclaim chain fires —
each ModuleEntry::Code drops, Arc<Jit> refcount hits 0,
custom Drop calls unsafe JITModule::free_memory() per batch.
